Don’t Starve Together: A Sonnet of Praise

Don’t Starve Together is a game without peer,
Where survival is the greatest challenge.
With friends or alone, you can explore
A world full of dangers and of wit.

You can choose from different characters,
Each with their own perks and flaws.
You can craft and build and gather,
And face the seasons and their laws.

The graphics are charming and unique,
The music is fitting and divine.
The gameplay is thrilling and mystique,
The fun is endless and fine.

Don’t Starve Together is a game to love,
A masterpiece that I can’t get enough.

For those who havent played dont starve, you're trying to survive in a surprisingly deeply simulated ecosystem that's illustrated like a Tim Burton cartoon. Lots of trial and experimentation is required (or else much perusing of the Wiki). It takes hundreds of hours to fully understand the world you're in.

The difficulty is that those who have played a lot of dont starve have so much more expertese than those who have never played it that it's the equivalent of a wilderness survival guide taking an 8 year old city kid camping.

There are PVP servers, avoid them if you arent experienced in the game, it's not the way most of us play it, but some people love it that way. New players joining these servers are fodder. Joining an open Co-op world you may be able to find someone to help you.

The only quibble is lack of goal or endgame content. In the base 'dont starve' you have 7 gates to pass through and a great mystery to solve (why they hell you're in this world in the first place).

The game is filled with quainltly beautiful struggles for survival, and benefits a lot from cooperation.

The game is very fun to play especially with friends, it has alot of content, such as bosses(Fuelweaver being one of the greatest), exploring new biomes/islands, crafting new stuff that can help you survive, Ancient Ruins, Lore and my favorite part, base building. Played with and without mods. Some tweaking to the gameplay is necessary if you don't want to rebuild your camp every two days, IMO. Beefalo's will chase you while in heat (I'm assuming that's what it means anyway, when their rear ends go red). Frogs will annoy you. Tentacles will slap you silly. Pigs are the happy go lucky ones, for the most part. Turkeys will be jerks and steal your berries. Mosquitos and bees will chase you. Spiders get butt hurt if you even go near their property. Basically, expect the unexpected, and don't expect to live very long at a time.

In other words? It's great. Can't wait for the full release, and I'm currently making sure all my friends get it.

Dont Starve, a really intriguing game with a gameplay that can appear at the beginning of the usual where the goal is to survive. Graphics could make the picky ones turn up their noses, but believe it or not in the long run, not tired and is very cool. The exploration within the game is infinite being the huge map leaving out the various caves and biomes within it. One of the main points of this game are the monsters, it is possible to meet any unimaginable creature from giants to mutant monsters. The gameplay presents a huge variety of possible crafts that can allow you to build huge and creative bases, in addition to this you will also find several protagonists with skills that will allow you to vary your experience, the fights are quite simple as soon as you get carried away, they are quite schematic, that is, they attack themselves and expect the enemy to do the same repeating it until it dies, so it might seem boring but the atmosphere and the monsters you meet will not disappoint you in expectations. Survival within the game is really tough in almost all biomes, especially during the winter and summer, not to mention when it rains.
To conclude, I really recommend this game to survival lovers.

I haven't played all of them, not even close, but I have to say that DST is kind of the only survival game that actually lives up to the promise of what a survival game is. There's a few things that separate it from most, but I think what makes it so replayable is the focus on resources. Most survival games have two, maybe three resources you need to keep track of, food, health, and sometimes stamina or disease or something like that. DST has the fascinatingly complex sanity mechanic, along with light, temperature, boss timers, and dozens of other conditional issues to keep track of, like wetness and enlightenment. It never feels overwhelming, but it DOES keep you on your toes, even as an experienced player. On my most recent run, I did an early ruins rush on WX-78 that I prepared for like a mofo. I had the *perfect* setup, using the moggle circuit for light, bringing tons of food and healing, materials for weapons and extra armor, but because I'm an idiot and forgot it can rain in winter if you're in the caves, I came within a hair's breadth of death after forgetting to bring wetness protection. That constant, real threat of losing everything you've built on the back of one crucial mistake is what makes your successes in the Constant so rewarding.
